pr_title: fix #5276 routes table hang using non-blocking read on netlink socket
pr_body: Linux Issue #5276 can be hard to reproduce in the wild, as it depends on recv() being called after all data has already been read.  I was able to reproduce it with a test program using readNetlink() and choosing a buffer size matching the amount of data my system was reporting (1324 bytes).  The issue here is doing a blocking read on a socket with no remaining data, which never returns.  I changed the recv to use MSG_DONTWAIT, and removed all of the NLMSG logic from readNetlink().
pr_comments: It also looks like a lot of error checking was removed, could you just comment for posterity (and because I'm not 100%) why it was all removed?

Some error checking was removed because it no longer needs to be done.  This PR separates reading of bytes from parsing the netlink messages.  The existing code was doing both together, making things more complicated than it needs to be.
